claims.text: The initial Hf-Mo-Ta-Ti-Zr alloy is single-phase BCC.
The asymmetric XRD peaks of the initial alloy arise from dendritic-versus-interdendritic compositional micro-segregation.
The initial alloy has low room-temperature fracture strain.
Adding approximately 4 at.% Cr induces a complex multicomponent Laves phase in Hf-Mo-Ta-Ti-Zr.
The Cr-induced Laves phase occupies approximately 4 vol.% of the alloy.
The Laves phase forms primarily in interdendritic regions.
The Laves phase has a reticulated, interconnected morphology.
The interconnected Laves phase forces cracks onto tortuous paths through crack deflection and branching.
Crack deflection and branching increase the fracture-surface area.
Lattice distortion caused by Cr solute atoms contributes to solid-solution hardening.
Cr addition contracts the BCC matrix lattice parameter.
Cr-induced lattice contraction reduces the lattice-mismatch energy.
Reduced lattice-mismatch energy limits the solid-solution-hardening efficacy of Cr relative to other solutes.
Cr addition produces a measurable increase in yield strength.
Laves-phase pinning contributes to the predicted yield-strength increase.
The Cr-modified alloy has decreased or stagnant room-temperature fracture strain relative to the baseline alloy.
The interconnected Laves network is brittle and can serve as a continuous crack path or stress concentrator.
The Cr-free baseline alloy has lower yield strength than the Cr-modified alloy.
The Cr-free baseline alloy has higher fracture strain than the Cr-modified alloy because it lacks the interconnected brittle Laves network.
If the Cr-induced lattice-parameter shift is expansive or negligible rather than contractive, solid-solution hardening may dominate and alter the predicted outcome.

contradictions.description: The same interconnected Laves morphology is described both as a crack-deflecting barrier that impedes crack extension and as a continuous brittle crack path or stress concentrator that promotes fracture. Competing effects are possible, but the hypothesis does not specify when or why one role dominates, weakening the causal account of the net fracture-strain decrease.
